description:
FILED s431 (Opus 5) by the P1 flip re-census.  s419 called this "family 4, #153 B3 residue"; B3 closed in s430 WITHOUT touching it (it was never B3 -- docs/plan-post-s430.md section 0 lists it as "by-design walker declines + PPI's $$ mislex"), so the family has had no open owner since.  13 census rows, 5 spellings, in 6 files.

1. `$${$_[0]}` -- t/op/gv.t 911,912 + t/uni/gv.t 805,806 (4 rows).
   PPI 1.291 lexes `$${$_[0]}` as Magic($$) + Block, i.e. the PID variable
   followed by a bare block; perl reads `${ ${$_[0]} }`.  Same family as
   docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md section 1 (`$$$ref` -> `$$` + `$ref`), one
   spelling further.  A space does not help (`$$ {$_[0]}` lexes the same).
   PROBE s431: `sub g { $${$_[0]} } my $x=5; my $r=\$x; print g(\$r), "\n";`
   perl 5, PCL drops the sub's only statement and prints nothing.

2. `++${"23::foo"}` -- t/op/universal.t 112, t/uni/method.t 193,194 (3 rows;
   the two uni rows are the same shape with a non-ASCII BYTE package name, so
   this is NOT a Unicode question -- it is an increment through a SYMBOLIC
   scalar ref).  PROBE s431: `++${"23::foo"}; print "v=", ${"23::foo"}, "\n";`
   perl v=1, PCL drops and prints `v=` (silent wrong).  Shares #461's rows.

3. `*X = *-;` / `*Y = *!;` -- t/re/reg_namedcapture.t 18,25 (2 rows).  A glob
   assigned from a PUNCTUATION glob.  Compiler reason: "Got op '-', not
   postfix.  But there is nothing after it??"  PROBE s431: `our $X; *X = *-;
   print "ok\n";` perl ok, PCL drops.

4. `local *a = *1;` -- t/re/subst.t 951,958 (2 rows).  A glob from a NUMERIC
   glob (the capture-group globs).  PROBE s431: valid perl, PCL drops.

5. `*{;undef} = 3` -- t/op/gv.t 1020 (1 row) and `*^R = *caretRglobwithnoscalar`
   -- t/re/pat.t 1715 (1 row).  The first is inside `eval { }` and the file
   asserts the DIE MESSAGE ("Can't use an undefined value as a symbol
   reference"), so PCL's drop loses an error-message row; the second is a
   CARET-named glob (the #412 caret-name machinery, other sigil).

ROW COST of the files today: op/gv.t 61, uni/gv.t 50, op/universal.t 75,
uni/method.t 23, re/reg_namedcapture.t 0, re/subst.t 0, re/pat.t 0.

SHAPE: (1) is a token repair (`_repair_*` in Pl/Parser2.pm, the established
pattern -- Magic($$) followed by a Cast-able `{` in TERM position is two
casts); (2) is a runtime/emission question (an lvalue through a symbolic
ref); (3)-(5) are the glob-value family, which is where #423's finding
("glob VALUE is glob REF in the box model") already sits -- measure the glob
representation before touching them.

BAR: the probes above vs perl + the inverse for each repair (a REAL `$$`
PID read: `print "$$\n"`; a real glob assignment `*bar = \&f`); gate-SET scan
over both populations for any repair; corpus-diff; guard rows.


MEASURED s440 (Fable), items 3-5: the glob REPRESENTATION is NOT the question -- `our $x=1; our @x=(1,2); *y = *x; print "$y|@y"; *z = \\$x; local *w = *x;` is byte-identical to perl.  All three drop at the PARSE: `*X = *-` -> "Got op '-', not postfix" (PPI: Cast `*` + Operator `-`), `local *a = *1` -> "Missing case: []" (Cast `*` + Number), `*{;undef} = 3` -> "Missing case: [Statement::Null<;>, Statement<undef>]".  So the fix is a TOKEN REPAIR in the #415/#451 family -- the sibling of Pl::Parser::_merge_punct_array_symbols for the `*` sigil (a punctuation or NUMERIC glob name after `*`), plus the `*{;EXPR}` block-deref spelling in the term walker -- not a runtime change.  Inverse probes the repair must keep: `*` as multiplication (`$a *-1`, `$a * -1`, `$n*1`, `2*!0`), `*{"name"}` / `*{$ref}` symbolic globs, `*STDOUT`.

ITEM 2 DONE (agent s441a, bf4f367) and ITEM 1 DONE (s441b, 94ae44d); merged by Fable s440.

Item 2 was not a missing feature but a precedence accident: Pl::PExpr::op_info calls every PPI Cast a one-operand prefix operator of precedence 90, and `++`/`--` (92) are the only prefix operators above it -- so the loop reduced the increment first and handed it the bare `$` cast as its whole operand. One predicate, Pl::PExpr::_is_prefix_op_token, now answers YES for a Cast, routing the pair through the loop's existing "adjacent prefix operators reduce INNER-first" walk. Every other prefix op is AT 90, where ties resolve rightmost -- which is why `\$$r` / `!$$r` / `-$$r` always worked. The family was wider than the filed shape: `++$$r`, `++${$r}`, `++${$n}`, `++${"main::z"}`, `++$$$rr`, `++${\ $l}` and all `--` twins. Two runtime defects rode with it (f588276): %p-accessor-place-p did not list p-cast-$/p-$ while the ++/-- macros always had, so `${"name"} += 2` was a SILENT NO-OP; and p-pre--'s setf-able arm was `(decf place)` where its p-pre++ twin numifies, so `--$$r` died on a box.

Item 1 was TWO stacked PPI errors: the PID Magic (repaired since s390) AND the braces structured as a Structure::Subscript, leaving `Cast Cast Subscript` -- a hash access with no base. The same pre-pass (_split_pid_magic_cast_run) now re-blesses those braces to Structure::Block. Adjacency stays the test (perl's own rule: `$$ {$r}` with a space is an element of %$ -- probed). Logged as docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md sec. 1b + a row in docs/ppi-bug-report.t (32 tests).

Measured: 528-file companion A/B DIFF = exactly op/universal.t, uni/method.t, op/gv.t, uni/gv.t (a PARSE ERROR becoming code); corpus-diff identical over 111 + 6 shapes; lib A/B SAME; op/universal.t C_ok 61 -> 79 (+18, the prediction); census 81/185 -> 78/178 by edit. Guard Pl/t/prefix-incr-deref-01.t (12 rows, 6 inverses), inverse-run on the base.

REMAINING: items 3, 4, 5 -- the glob-value family. MEASURED s440 (Fable, above): the representation is not the question; all three drop at the PARSE (a `*` followed by a punctuation char / a number / `{;EXPR}`) -- a token repair in the #415/#451 family. Residue filed: #505 (`${NUMBER}` is not a symbolic ref), #506 (`$$ {EXPR}` with a space -> unbound `%$` at load), #507 (`$$$_` still dropped: the repair's next-token test accepts Token::Symbol, not Token::Magic).
ITEMS 3+4 DONE and ITEM 5 DONE-IN-PART, s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5).

ITEM 3+4 (`*X = *-`, `*Y = *!`, `local *a = *1`) -- the s440 measurement was
right: a TOKEN REPAIR, and the representation was never the question.
Pl::Parser2::_repair_punct_glob_name rewrites the name into the SYMBOLIC
spelling the compiler already lowers -- `*-` -> `*{'-'}` -- and reparses.
Probed first: `*-` and `*{"-"}` are the same glob in perl even inside a
package (both reach the forced-main punctuation globals), and `*1` /
`*{"1"}` both alias $1; PCL matches perl byte-for-byte on the symbolic
spellings today.  ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§26 + two rows in ppi-bug-report.t
(now 36).

THE CONDITION IS A WHITELIST, NOT `_ends_term`'s NEGATIVE, and that is the
finding.  A false positive turns working multiplication into a glob and kills
the file, while a miss costs only today's drop (the standing asymmetry rule).
And `_ends_term` is WRONG here: `@{$h} * (â¦)` reads as term position because a
deref block's `}` is not a subscript's (io/through.t:33 proves it).  So the
repair fires only where a `*` can OPEN a glob name: statement/list start
(`;` `{` `(` `[`), after `=`, `,` or `=>`, after `return`.  Measured over all
four populations: 1329 files, 23 term-position `*` sites, the whitelist
selects exactly the 8 glob ones -- the other 15 are glob PATTERNS inside a
`<â¦>` run PPI derailed (`<op/*.t>`, `<*>`), regex bodies in t/re/pat.t, and
that deref-block multiplication.

`local` IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE WHITELIST.  `local *1 = sub {â¦}`
(t/op/method.t:38, t/op/tie_fetch_count.t:203) would become `local *{'1'} =
sub {â¦}`, and _process_local_declaration's typeglob branch matches a
Token::Symbol only -- a Cast+Block target falls through and the statement
VANISHES with no announcement (task #564; the `local *{"1"}` spelling loses it
at HEAD too).  Trading a loud drop for a silent one is the wrong direction, so
that shape keeps dropping until #564 closes.  `local *a = *1` is unaffected
(its `*1` is on the right of the `=`).

ITEM 5, first half (`*{;undef} = 3`, t/op/gv.t:1020) -- NOT a lexer bug at
all.  PPI keeps perl's `;` disambiguator as a PPI::Statement::Null child of
the Block, and the walker had no case for a two-child deref block, so
`${;"a"}`, `@{;"z"}` and `*{;undef}` were ALL dropped -- one message, three
sigils.  Pl::Parser2::_normalize_null_statements deletes it.  TWO traps paid
for on the way:
  (a) PPI::Statement::Null is INSIGNIFICANT, so `schildren` cannot see it --
      a first version guarded on `schildren > 1` and changed nothing;
  (b) THE `;` MEANS MORE THAN "THIS IS A BLOCK".  Inside a forced block a lone
      bareword is an EXPRESSION; in a plain deref it is the NAME.  Probed
      (`sub foo { "bar" } our $bar = 5; our $foo = 9`): `${foo}` is 9,
      `${;foo}` is 5 == `${ foo() }`, `*{foo}` is *main::foo, `*{;foo}` is
      *main::bar.  Deleting the Null alone emitted
      `(p-glob-assign-dynamic "undef" 3)` -- the glob literally named "undef",
      a SILENT WRONG where a loud drop had been.  The bareword is therefore
      made an explicit call before the `;` goes.
And the die: `%p-check-symbol-reference` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp makes
`*{EXPR}` with an UNDEF EXPR die as perl does, on both sides of an assignment
(`*{undef()} = 3` and `my $x = *{undef()}`); an EMPTY STRING is legal and is
NOT the same thing (probed).  Rule 12: without it, un-dropping the statement
would have traded the loud drop for a silent no-op, and op/gv.t:1020 asserts
the message.

ITEM 5, second half (`*^R = *g`) NOT DONE -> task #562, with `*]`
(t/op/tie_fetch_count.t:189, where PPI makes the `]` a Structure token).
`^R` is perl's caret convention for chr(18), not the glob named `^`, so it
needs the #412 caret-name machinery -- and PCL's `$^R` is itself inert
(task #565), so the glob half alone buys nothing.

RESIDUE FILED: #561 (a glob alias to a MAGIC punctuation variable yields an
empty slot -- `*Y = *!` then `$Y` reads ""; and `%!` is not implemented at all,
an unbound CL variable that kills the file), #562, #564, #565.
t/re/reg_namedcapture.t now produces two honest `not ok` rows where it used to
abort at the drop (0 ok / 2 notok) -- the s435-flip pattern again: a fix that
makes values real exposes what was failing invisibly.

GUARD: Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t (8 rows, inverse-run: 8/8 fail with the
repairs gated off).
subject: GLOB SURGERY / SYMBOLIC REF: 13 of the s431 census's 31 gap rows are one family -- `$${EXPR}` (PPI reads `$$` as the PID), `*X = *-`, `local *a = *1`, `*{;undef}`, `*^R = *g`, `++${"..."}`
